item.title: Kagoshima Cherry Blossoms — Guide
item.description: Kagoshima’s warm southern location means it is one of the earliest places on mainland Japan to see cherry blossoms (sakura) each spring, with trees often in full bloom from around late March. When the blossoms arrive, the city and surrounding areas host a much-loved hanami (blossom-viewing) season and festivals. Cherry trees bloom at numerous spots across the prefecture: in city parks and along riversides, around the ruins of Tsurumaru Castle, in the beautiful garden of Sengan-en (where the pink blossoms frame views of the smoking Sakurajima volcano across the bay), and at scenic viewpoints and mountain areas.

item.title: Ohara Festival — Guide
item.description: The Ohara Festival (Ohara Matsuri) is Kagoshima city’s largest and liveliest festival, held every year in early November. Its centrepiece is a huge mass street dance in which around 20,000 participants — organised into teams from companies, schools and community groups, dressed in matching happi coats, yukata and colourful costumes — dance together down the city’s main streets to the infectious rhythm of local folk songs, above all the famous ‘Ohara-bushi’.

item.title: Sakurajima Volcano — Guide
item.description: Sakurajima is one of the world’s most active volcanoes and the iconic symbol of Kagoshima, looming dramatically across Kinko Bay from the city. This towering volcanic peak erupts frequently — sometimes puffing plumes of ash over the city daily — and a lava flow in 1914 was so vast it joined the former island to the Osumi Peninsula. Despite its fury, people live on its slopes, and it’s easily and safely visited by a short, scenic ferry from Kagoshima city (running 24 hours).

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Kagoshima: Ibusuki, Kirishima & Sakurajima
item.description: Kagoshima Prefecture — Japan’s volcanic southern gateway — sits at the tip of Kyushu with active volcanoes, subtropical islands, and some of Japan’s most distinctive onsen experiences. Ibusuki offers the world’s only natural sand bath (sunamushi) powered by geothermal heat, Kirishima provides highland volcanic resort scenery, and Sakurajima volcano dominates the entire region’s skyline. Best Areas to Stay Kagoshima City — Sakurajima Views The prefectural capital faces the active Sakurajima volcano across a narrow bay — ash occasionally falls on the city, which locals consider normal.
